_note: Every request this phone builds, as one shared fixture for two test suites.
The Kotlin half (AgentdRequestWireTest) asserts that `Agentd`'s builders
produce exactly these, so a builder that changes shape is caught. The Rust
half (rime-agent-core/tests/android_requests_wire.rs) deserializes each one
into `rime_agent_core::protocol::Request` and asserts the variant, so a
request the phone sends that the daemon cannot parse is caught too.
That second half is the guard this unit needed and did not have. Two
separate rounds of work were built on the claim that `worktrees` was not a
verb — a claim read off `request.rs`'s privileged-operation `Verb` instead
of off `protocol.rs`'s wire `Request`. A fixture the daemon's own serde
must accept cannot be wrong about which verbs exist: a verb that is not
there fails to deserialize, and a verb that is there and spelled wrong
fails too.
`decide` is deliberately absent and must stay absent. privilege.rs:1176
refuses it from any non-local origin before the pending check, so a phone
can neither approve nor deny, and a builder for it would be a builder for a
request that is always refused. See Approvals.kt.
`projects` and `profiles` are NEW, and the note that used to stand in
StartAgentScreen.kt said neither existed. That was true when it was
written. They exist now, and the reason they are two verbs rather than
fields on an existing one is cost: `worktrees` runs git in every
remembered project, including `merge-tree --write-tree`, so a picker that
asked it on screen open would put seconds of git between a tap and a text
field. `projects` reads one small JSON record per project and runs no
subprocess; `profiles` stats a table of paths and the PATH. A client asks
those two to build the picker and asks `worktrees` only for the project
the user chose.
`profiles` is the verb that retires a guess. `Agentd.commandIsRequired`
used to hard-code `id == "generic"` because the daemon published no
flag, and its own comment said so. The flag is `command_required` and the
daemon derives it from the adapter table, so an adapter added later that
needs a program named by the caller needs no app release.
`input` has ONE builder and one door, and that is the point. A typed reply,
a push-to-talk transcript and a clipboard send all reach the wire through
the SAME builder, because they all reach it through Reply.plan and
Reply.check. Voice and clipboard put text in the reply box for a person to
read; Send is what terminates it. A second send path would be a second
place for the recycled-session-id guard to be forgotten, and forgetting it
types somebody's sentence into a stranger's terminal. See Handoff.kt.
It has several SHAPES now, and each is here. `input` is the single write
that ends in CR, which is what a bare return still is and what every reply
used to be. It typed and did not submit: measured 2026-09-30 against Claude
Code 2.1.283, a long burst ending in CR is read as a paste and the CR
becomes a newline. So a reply's Return is now a separate write:
`input_submit` against a daemon whose hello lists `input_submit` (the
daemon writes the CR 80 ms later), and against an older one the text
alone, 100 ms on the phone, then `input_bare`. The exact JSON is
docs/remote-live-contract.md section 1.2.
`rename` and `peek` are contract sections 1.5 and 1.6. `rename_clear` is
the one request here that carries an explicit null, and deliberately: the
null IS the instruction (no name any more), the opposite of `revoke_all`,
where the absent key is. `remote_hello` is NOT here and must not be:
rime-remoted answers it itself, like push_register, and this fixture is
what rime-agentd must parse.
`receive` is the SECOND takeover verb and never travels as a control
frame. It is here because this fixture is about what the daemon parses,
and it is the request Upload puts in a Frame.Open — rime-remoted refuses
it on channel zero exactly as it refuses `attach` there.
The note that used to stand here said there is no file-upload verb, and
gave the arithmetic: a Frame::Control carries at most MAX_PAYLOAD = 65514
bytes, base64 costs 4/3, so a single-frame handoff tops out near 48 KB
while a screenshot is 100 KB to 2 MB. Every number is right and the
conclusion did not follow, because all of it measures ONE frame type.
Open/Data/Close is begin/chunk/end, wire.rs says so in its own words, and
Frame::data_frames has been chunking every PTY byte this phone has ever
received. What was missing was a sink to chunk into, and that is the verb
below.
`clipboard` READS THE COMPUTER'S clipboard, and the line that used to
stand here — 'there is still NO clipboard-read verb' — is no longer true.
It is the receive half of P1-059's third criterion and the opposite
direction from `input`: `input` carries the PHONE's clipboard to the
computer, this carries the computer's to the phone. It takes no `id`,
because one Wayland seat has one clipboard and there is nothing to name,
which also means it is not a session action and must not be offered from
a screen that exists only while a session is waiting. Unlike `receive` it
does NOT take the channel over: proxy::takes_over_the_channel is `attach`
and `receive` and nothing else, so it is an ordinary control frame.
